items.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021
items.q: Well naturally it’s all the American Songbook. Gershwin, Cole Porter, you know, Sophisticated — Duke Ellington. We played the same songs...

ctx.x: If I could go back in time and drop in on a gig that you were on when you were about fifteen with the family band and write down every tune that you played, what would some of those titles be?

Well naturally it’s all the American Songbook. Gershwin, Cole Porter, you know, Sophisticated — Duke Ellington. We played the same songs that I played the major portion of my livelihood for 62 years, you understand? The same songs. Now funny story, my father, in other words we traveled because we worked all in the immediate area, the towns in Pennsylvania, say for instance I don’t know if you’d call it a territory band, but we’d travel maybe forty, fifty miles to Emporium, Pennsylvania or the Wellsville © Fillius…

Country Club and all of these various things, and back. And so we traveled in a car and you had an upright bass and the sound system and a set of drums so you’d all get in one car and go to the gig. And we’d set up and, but my father after setting up the drums, every time he’d say, “Oh what are we going to play? What are we going to play?” Uh, “Almost Like Being in Love.” Because he’d call the same tune every night. And he would say it and play an intro and then he’d sing the song and the party was on.
